thread:
alex.w: quick summary: ran kv-cache prefetch + eviction sweep across regions and GPUs this morning. goal was hit-rate vs p50/p99 tradeoffs for mixed seqlen workloads. results look noisy but there's a clear region+gpu pattern.

perf-bot: automatic benchmark upload complete: https://bench.internal/redwood/kv-prefetch/1826549876 (csv + charts) :white_check_mark:

maya.r: nice — which seqlen distribution did you use? synthetic or sampled traces?

alex.w: sampled traces from prod routing logs (anonymized) — mix: 0-64: 72%, 65-256: 22%, 257-1024: 6%. also ran a heavy-tail variant (power law alpha=2.3).

kevin_g: can you paste the headline numbers (hitrate / p50 / p99) for h100 vs a100 in us-west and apac? curious about p99 tailing when eviction aggressive.

alex.w: sure. top-level table (prefetch window=64, eviction_policy=lru_age):
- h100 us-west: hitrate 81%, p50 28ms, p99 120ms
- a100 us-west: hitrate 76%, p50 34ms, p99 200ms
- h100 apac: hitrate 78%, p50 32ms, p99 150ms
- a100 apac: hitrate 70%, p50 40ms, p99 320ms (observed paging spikes)

jonas_m: that apac a100 p99 is bad. was that with paging to host enabled?

alex.w: yes — we allowed paging to CPU for eviction overflow. the p99 spikes correlate with page-in events (see perf chart). when we disabled paging (fail instead), we got OOMs but p99 dropped to ~190ms for the surviving requests.

maya.r: interesting. how did eviction threshold affect hit rate? can we tune a knee point?

alex.w: quick sweep for eviction_threshold: 0.2,0.35,0.5 (prefetch=64):
- thr=0.2 => hitrate 62%, p99 260ms
- thr=0.35 => hitrate 75%, p99 150ms
- thr=0.5 => hitrate 82%, p99 140ms
So lower threshold reduces hitrate and increases p99 (more paging). but raising too high increases memory pressure and OOM risk on smaller GPUs.

kevin_g: what about prefetch window size? any diminishing returns?

alex.w: yes. moving from 32->64 gave +9% hitrate avg, 64->128 gave +3% but increased vram by ~12%. 256 had marginal gains and caused a few allocations to fail on a100 in apac.

jonas_m: kernel choices? did you try the new 'streamed-kv' kernel vs the 'baseline' kernels?

alex.w: tested both. streamed-kv uses async prefetch and had lower p99 on h100 (p99 down ~18%) but on a100 its async scheduling contended with other workloads and latency sometimes regressed. suggestion: pick kernel by region/gpu profile: h100 -> streamed-kv, a100 -> baseline/optimized-legacy.

maya.r: any capacity guidance? if a customer runs this mixed seqlen traffic in apac on a100, what's a conservative sizing multiplier vs h100?

alex.w: empirically ~1.5x throughput gap for identical configs. so for capacity sizing start with 1.5x tokens/sec requirement and validate with tail-focused probes. also prefer larger eviction_threshold or bigger prefetch on a100 to avoid paging.

kevin_g: can you share the config snippet you used so we can reproduce?

alex.w: sure:
```kv:
  prefetch_window: 64
  eviction_policy: lru_age
  eviction_threshold: 0.45
  fallback_to_paging: true
  paging_target: host
  kernel_select:
    h100: streamed-kv
    a100: optimized-legacy
```

maya.r: let's re-run with the heavy-tail trace and prefetch=128 but set fallback_to_paging=false on apac a100 to surface OOMs. want to see if evict_thr=0.5 + prefetch=128 keeps hitrate high without paging.

alex.w: scheduled a targeted rerun for tonight across apac/us-west with those params. tagging @kevin_g & @jonas_m to review the follow-up.

perf-bot: rerun scheduled: job id kv-sweep-1826550105, ETA 10h. artifacts will be posted to the same bench URL. :rocket:

kevin_g: thanks — will check after run. if apac still spikes we should consider region-specific kernel fallbacks at runtime. :thumbsup:

maya.r: +1. can we also add a synthetic 'uniform-long' test (all seqlen 512) to stress test paging paths?

alex.w: added to the matrix. I'll post the condensed results (one-pager) when the jobs finish.
